Web search results for ""oldest flavor" "flavor graveyard" ben jerry's":

The **oldest flavor** in the Ben & Jerry's **Flavor Graveyard** is **Dastardly Mash**.[1][2][3] 

While Ben & Jerry's first-ever flavor was Vanilla (created in 1978 and still sold today) and their original eight pint flavors from 1978 (such as Oreo Mint and Honey Coffee) have all been discontinued, **Dastardly Mash** (produced from **1979 to 1991**) is the oldest retired flavor to have a dedicated headstone in the graveyard.

### Key Facts about Dastardly Mash:
*   **Ingredients:** Chocolate ice cream with pecans, almonds, raisins, and chocolate chips.
*   **Claim to Fame:** It is the only flavor in Ben & Jerry's history to ever contain raisins.
*   **Headstone Rhyme:** 
    > "Here the brazen
    > DASTARDLY lies.
    > Some say that raisin,
    > Caused its demise."[3]

### About the Flavor Graveyard:
*   **Location:** The physical graveyard is located on a hill overlooking the Ben & Jerry's factory in **Waterbury, Vermont**.[4]
*   **History:** It opened in **1997** with four original residents: Dastardly Mash, Economic Crunch, Ethan Almond, and Tuskegee Chunk.[5]
*   **Current Status:** There are now over 35 physical headstones in Vermont and many more in the "digital" graveyard on the company's website. Each headstone features a witty epitaph explaining why the flavor was "de-pinted."[4]
*   **Resurrections:** Occasionally, fans can vote to "resurrect" a flavor from the graveyard for a limited time (e.g., *Dublin Mudslide* was famously brought back).[3]

import urllib.request
import re

flavors = [
    "schweddy-balls", "wavy-gravy", "fossil-fuel", "turtle-soup", "vermonty-python",
    "this-is-nuts", "aloha-macadamia", "chocolate-comfort", "chocolate-chip-cookie-dough-frozen-yogurt",
    "sugar-plum", "ethan-almond", "peanut-butter-and-jelly", "bovinity-divinity", "miz-jelenas-sweet-potato-pie",
    "urban-jumble", "creme-brulee", "rainforest-crunch", "cool-britannia", "oh-pear",
    "fresh-georgia-peach", "peanuts-popcorn", "tuskeegee-chunk", "white-russian", "economic-crunch",

    "holy-cannoli", "tennessee-mud", "coconutterly-fair", "chocolate-macadamia", "cow-power", "dublin-mudslide"
]

for flavor in flavors:
    url = f"https://web.archive.org/web/20221127162426/https://www.benjerry.com/flavors/flavor-graveyard/{flavor}"
    try:
        req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={'User-Agent': 'Mozilla/5.0'})
        html = urllib.request.urlopen(req).read().decode('utf-8')
        years_match = re.search(r'>(\d{4})\s*-\s*(\d{4})<', html)
        if years_match:
            print(f"{flavor}: {years_match.group(1)} - {years_match.group(2)}")
        else:
            # Maybe search for just 4 digits
            print(f"{flavor}: no match")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"{flavor}: {e}")

EOF

The Ben & Jerry's **Flavor Graveyard** in Waterbury, Vermont, features granite headstones for discontinued flavors.[1][2] **Dastardly Mash** and **Economic Crunch** were two of the original four flavors memorialized when the physical graveyard opened in 1997 (alongside *Ethan Almond* and *Tuskegee Chunk*).[2][3][4][1][5]

### The Headstones[6][1][4][7][3][2][5][8][9][10]
*   **Dastardly Mash (1979–1991):** Chocolate ice cream with pecans, almonds, raisins, and chocolate chips.[5][4][9][2][6]

*   **Economic Crunch (1987–1987):** Vanilla ice cream with chocolate-covered almonds, pecans, and walnuts.[10][9][2][8][4]
    *   *Epitaph:[9][10][2][6][4][8][7][1][3][5]* "A delightful mash, This flavor we remember. For the stock market crash. On the sixth of November."

In the graveyard, these headstones are often seen in the same row or cluster because they were part of the inaugural "burial."[2] They are grey granite markers with rounded tops, set behind a white picket fence on a grassy hill.[2]
